questions.question: Describe how a green plant makes its own food. (3 marks)

points.description: Names the process as photosynthesis, happening in the leaf/chloroplasts using chlorophyll
points.exemplar: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of leaf cells, which contain chlorophyll.

points.description: States the raw materials: carbon dioxide and water
points.exemplar: The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil.

points.description: States the product glucose is made using light energy
points.exemplar: Using light energy, the plant converts these into glucose and releases oxygen.

demo_answers.text: Plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose in their chloroplasts, using chlorophyll.

test_answers.text: Plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose in their chloroplasts, using chlorophyll.
Photosynthesis happens in the leaves. Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight and the plant uses carbon dioxide and water to make its own food (glucose).
The plant takes in CO2 and water, and with light energy from the sun it produces sugar. This happens in the chloroplast which has chlorophyll in it.
Plants photosynthesise using sunlight to make glucose.
The plant absorbs carbon dioxide and water from its surroundings to grow.
Chlorophyll in the leaf captures light so the plant can make its food.
Plants get bigger because they drink water and grow towards the sun.
Plants eat soil to get nutrients and energy to survive.

questions.question: Explain why a car needs a bigger force to start moving from rest than it does to keep moving at a steady speed. (2 marks)

points.description: Identifies friction as the force opposing motion (static friction is larger)
points.exemplar: Static friction between the tyres and the road opposes the car starting to move, and static friction is larger than moving friction.

points.description: Explains that once moving, only a smaller force is needed to overcome (dynamic) friction and keep it at steady speed
points.exemplar: Once the car is moving, a smaller force is needed to overcome friction and keep the resultant force at zero for a steady speed.

demo_answers.text: Static friction is greater than moving friction, so more force is needed to start than to keep the car moving at a steady speed where forces are balanced.

test_answers.text: Static friction is greater than moving friction, so more force is needed to start than to keep the car moving at a steady speed where forces are balanced.
Friction opposes the car starting to move and is stronger when the car is still. Once moving, a smaller force can overcome the friction and keep the speed steady.
There is more friction to overcome when the car is not yet moving, so a bigger force is needed at the start.
Once the car is moving, the forces are balanced so it stays at a steady speed with less force.
The engine is stronger at the start of the journey than later on.
The car uses more petrol when it starts moving.
